articles.excerpt: The headline people click in Google. Put your main keyword and the city near the front, and keep it short so it doesn't get cut off. The short text under the title in search results. It doesn't help y…
articles.body: On-page SEO is everything you control on the page itself. Here's the whole list, one or two lines each. Tomorrow I'll go through every one properly. 1. Title tag The headline people click in Google. Put your main keyword and the city near the front, and keep it short so it doesn't get cut off. 2. Meta description The short text under the title in search results. It doesn't help you rank directly, but a good one gets you more clicks. 3. URL Short and readable. /dentist-kaithal beats /page?id=4821 . 4. Headings One H1 that says what the page is. Use H2s and H3s to break the rest into sections. 5. Content Answer exactly what the person searched for, in plain words. If the answer is buried, rewrite it. 6. Keywords Use your main keyword naturally in the title, the H1 and the first paragraph.

articles.body: TL;DR what: Google, with Japan's National Police Agency, Lumen, HUMAN Security, Plume, Synthient and TrendAI, took down the control servers of a 1.3 million-device Android botnet and says Shenzhen device maker Videostrong intentionally built the x.cpe backdoor into its boxes. impact: Operators could silently install apps, run commands, capture screens, steal account details and open reverse shells, and criminal buyers turned the boxes into residential proxies and ad fraud engines across 206 models. fix: There is no patch: x.cpe lives in firmware signed with the maker's key and reinstalls on reboot, so TrendAI says cleanup needs vendor action, platform protection or device replacement, while Google has banned Videostrong from certified Android.

articles.title: I Built LLM Explained: 43 Interactive Pages That Take You From Tokens to AI Agents
articles.excerpt: I kept running into the same problem while learning about large language models. I'd read a blog post about attention, nod along, and two days later I couldn't tell you why we divide by √d_k. I'd see…
articles.body: I kept running into the same problem while learning about large language models. I'd read a blog post about attention, nod along, and two days later I couldn't tell you why we divide by √d_k. I'd see "GQA", "MLA", "MoE", "LoRA", "HNSW" or "context rot" in a paper or a tweet, open five tabs, and close them all with the uneasy feeling that I sort of got it. And the field keeps moving, so there's always a new term on top of the ones I hadn't really nailed down. So I built the resource I wished I had: LLM Explained . It's a free, interactive course that goes from "why did RNNs hit a wall?" all the way to "how does a production agent retrieve, reason, act and get evaluated?" I built it to learn, and writing each page forced me to understand things properly.
articles.author: amananandrai

articles.title: Why UI Tests Break Every Sprint (and What an AI Testing Agent Changes)
articles.excerpt: The problem most test suites share Almost every team that automates UI testing hits the same wall. The suite starts small and works well. Then the product grows, the interface changes, and a growing s…
articles.body: The problem most test suites share Almost every team that automates UI testing hits the same wall. The suite starts small and works well. Then the product grows, the interface changes, and a growing share of your week goes to fixing tests that fail even though the application works fine. This is not a discipline problem. It comes from how most automated tests are built. Why traditional UI tests are brittle A typical scripted UI test identifies elements by locators : IDs, CSS selectors, XPath expressions. For example: driver . find_element ( By . CSS_SELECTOR , " #checkout > div.row:nth-child(2) > button.btn-primary " ). click () This line says nothing about what the user is trying to do. It describes where a button currently sits in the page structure.

articles.title: Find Duplicate Files in the Browser: SHA-256 Groups, Not Uploads
articles.excerpt: Duplicate files are rarely duplicates by name. They are duplicates by content — the same photo saved three times with three different names, the same export saved again by an older tool. So the useful…
articles.body: Duplicate files are rarely duplicates by name. They are duplicates by content — the same photo saved three times with three different names, the same export saved again by an older tool. So the useful question is not "do these two files look the same" but "do these two files hash the same". That is a question you can answer exactly, and you can answer it without handing your files to anybody. I work on OnePassApps, and the File Studio in our browser app has a Find duplicates tab that does precisely this. It hashes the content of the files you pick, groups the ones that match, and leaves every file where it is. What the panel says Open the File Studio and pick the Find duplicates tab. The empty panel is small and specific: 01 Source 0 files · 0 B. Only the files you choose are compared.

articles.title: James Webb Space Telescope uncovers new clues about the origins of 'interstellar invader' comet 3I/ATLAS
articles.excerpt: The findings are another clue towards understanding the origins of 3I/ATLAS and the planet-forming conditions around other stars.
articles.body: Using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), scientists have found that the interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS was built from tiny grains of ice mixed with dust that are quite different from the solar system’s comets. These ice grains do, however, bear striking similarities to some icy bodies located at the edge of the solar system, beyond the orbit of Neptune, so-called trans-Neptunian objects (TNOs). 3I/ATLAS was discovered entering the solar system in the summer of 2025. It was only the third object found entering the solar system from farther afield in the Milky Way after 1I/'Oumuamua , seen in 2017, and 2I/Borisov , detected in 2019. This meant the interstellar comet offered a rare chance to glimpse the conditions under which such bodies form in other star systems.

articles.title: Raising the quality of insights in agentic analytics
articles.excerpt: In just a few years, generative AI has changed the face of enterprise analytics, notably by making analytics accessible to users across the organization. Agentic AI promises to do even more, by automa…
articles.body: In just a few years, generative AI has changed the face of enterprise analytics, notably by making analytics accessible to users across the organization. Agentic AI promises to do even more, by automating entire workflows and taking actions based on agent insights. But there is a problem: The quality of insights that agents currently generate leaves much to be desired. Fewer than half of agent-generated insights at the organizations surveyed for this report lead to business improvement. And while most respondents praise the quality of their agents’ descriptive insights, reviews of their prescriptive insights—those on which actions are based—are decidedly mixed.
